eng_translation: Omeprazole is a proton pump inhibitor (PPI) used to reduce stomach acid production. It is commonly prescribed for conditions such as gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD), peptic ulcer disease, and Zollinger-Ellison syndrome. Omeprazole works by inhibiting the enzyme in the stomach wall that produces acid, thereby decreasing the amount of acid secreted into the stomach. It is available in both prescription and over-the-counter formulations and is typically taken once daily. Long-term use of PPIs may be associated with potential side effects, including nutrient deficiencies and an increased risk of certain infections.

Omeprazole works by inhibiting the action of proton pumps in the stomach, which are responsible for acid secretion. It is available in both prescription and over-the-counter forms and is typically taken once daily. Common side effects may include headache, diarrhea, and abdominal pain, although many people do not experience significant side effects. It is important to follow the prescribed dosage and duration of treatment to ensure effectiveness and minimize potential side effects. If you have any questions or concerns about omeprazole, it is recommended to consult with a healthcare provider.
